cards.text: Right before this, the prophet Isaiah told about the LORD's Servant, who bore the sin of many (Isaiah 53:12). Now the LORD speaks. And He's talking to a barren woman, one who has never had a child.

cards.question: A woman who has never had children. What does the LORD tell her to do?
The LORD says the desolate woman will have more children than the woman who has a husband.

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to the barren woman's tent, the place she calls home. I lived in a junk drawer for YEARS, friend, so I get real emotional about anybody's housing situation.

cards.question: If more children are coming, what does the LORD tell the barren woman to do with her tent?

cards.text: Stretch out the curtains, lengthen the ropes, drive the stakes in deep, do not hold back! That's the energy of somebody who just heard the WHOLE family is coming for the holidays and is pulling folding chairs out of every closet in the house.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say the woman needs all that extra room?

answers.text: She will spread out right and left
A great storm is coming her way
Her old tent will soon fall apart

cards.text: Her descendants will dispossess the nations and move right into the desolate cities. Then the LORD brings up the shame of her youth, and friend, everybody's got a few years they'd rather nobody pulled out of the photo album.

cards.question: The LORD tells the woman she will carry the shame of her youth for the rest of her life.

cards.text: She'll also remember no more the reproach of her widowhood. Then the LORD tells her who her husband is, and friend, hold onto your apron.

cards.question: The LORD says the woman will remember no more the reproach of her widowhood. Who does He say her husband is?

cards.text: Her Maker, the LORD of Hosts, the Holy One of Israel, her Redeemer, called the God of all the earth. She went from widow to THAT, and I thought going from a junk drawer to a gold base was a glow-up.

cards.question: The LORD says He has called the woman back, like a wife ___ and wounded in spirit.
Then the LORD talks about a time He forsook her: For a brief ___ I forsook you, but with ___ compassion I will bring you back.
The LORD says He hid His face from the woman in a surge of anger, and His kindness toward her will last only for a moment.

cards.text: Then the LORD brings up Noah, who went into the ark with his family because of the flood (Genesis 7:7), and says that to Him, this is like the days of Noah. I did years shut in tight with a crowd too, friend, except my crowd was rubber bands and dead batteries.

cards.question: Back in the days of Noah, what did the LORD swear?

answers.text: The waters would never again cover the earth
Rain would never again fall on the earth
Every mountain would be made low forever

cards.text: Like that oath, the LORD has sworn He will not be angry with her or rebuke her. Me, I once swore I'd stop stamping crooked when I get excited, and I made it about ONE batch.

cards.question: Even if the mountains are removed and the hills are shaken, the LORD says His loving devotion will not depart from her.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks to an afflicted city, lashed by storms, without solace. Storms and no comfort, friend, I know that one: years in a drawer where the only weather was dust, and the forecast was MORE dust.

cards.question: What does the LORD say He will build the afflicted city out of?

cards.text: Stones set in antimony, foundations of sapphires, pinnacles of rubies, gates of sparkling jewels. I get excited when somebody shines up my apron, and this city gets RUBIES on top.

cards.question: After the jeweled walls, the LORD talks about the city's sons. He says only a few of them will be taught by the LORD.

cards.text: All her sons taught by the LORD, great prosperity, established in righteousness, far from oppression. Friend, I got taught by the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, and all they ever taught me was how to argue.

cards.question: The LORD says the city will have no fear. What does He say about terror?

answers.text: It will not come near her
It will come back one day
It will camp outside her walls

cards.text: Now, somebody might still try something. The LORD says if anyone attacks her, it is not from Him.

cards.question: The LORD says whoever assails the city will ___ before her.

cards.text: Then the LORD talks about the craftsman who fans the coals into flame and forges a weapon fit for its task. I know a thing or two about fanning heat, friend, but my oven makes cookies, not weapons.

cards.question: The LORD says He is the One who created the craftsman who forges weapons.

cards.text: And He created the destroyer to wreak havoc, too. The guy at the forge AND the guy wrecking everything, the LORD made BOTH, and I'm over here proud I made a cookie box with a lid that closes.

cards.question: What does the LORD say happens to any weapon formed against the city?

answers.text: It will be handed to her

cards.text: And every tongue that accuses her, she will refute. That's walking into the meeting where somebody's blaming you, and you've already got the email with the timestamp.

cards.question: The LORD sums it all up. He says this is the heritage of whom?
The LORD says the servants of the LORD will have to win their own vindication.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the exact unseen wording of Isaiah 54:6. The preceding cards stop at Isaiah 54:5 and provide no storyteller setup about the deserted wife, so this is a next-word fill-in rather than a question about the passage's movement or meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Both blanks ask the baker to supply the exact wording of an unseen line from Isaiah 54:7. There is no preceding story card establishing this moment, so the baker is filling in the prophet's words rather than reasoning through a setup.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The stop ends without ever mentioning the LORD's promise in Isaiah 54:10 that His covenant of peace will not be broken. Card 19 covers His loving devotion, but the unbroken covenant of peace is another central promise in that verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
